title: fix(plugin-auth): a SCIM PATCH of only the name parts recomposes a derived display name
body:
Fixes #32380
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读
- 用户能看到什么变化:企业身份系统(Okta、Entra)只改员工的名或姓时,控制台显示的姓名现在随之更新;单独设定、与名和姓不同的显示名保持不变。
- 为什么做:属于企业单点登录与用户同步,替只同步名和姓的租户解决旧名长期不变的问题,按维护者「现在临时修、同时修源头」的裁决执行。
- 出错会怎样:只同步名或姓的租户会看到显示名被改成「名 姓」;去掉这个临时补丁即可直接撤回到原来的行为。
- 要你做什么:确认下文「边界情况」可以接受(身份系统明确发来、但恰好等于「名 姓」的显示名,改名时也会被重新拼接,供应商自己的测试要求保留它),然后把文末上游草稿提交给供应商。

## What changes

- `patches/@better-auth__scim@1.7.12.patch` (new, written with `pnpm patch` / `pnpm patch-commit`): a TEMPORARY vendor patch by maintainer ruling record 6845302116 (option C), with a header naming the ruling and its removal condition. In `setNamePart`, it recomposes `name.formatted` (and, through the vendor's own `setFormattedName`, `displayName`) with the vendor's own `composeName` when `name.formatted` equalled `composeName` of the parts before the part changed. Four lines in `dist/index.mjs`; nothing else in the package moves.
- `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: the `patchedDependencies` row beside the three existing patches, plus a note in the block's comment (ruling, what it fixes, who receives it, removal condition). `patch-commit` wrote the key into `package.json`'s `pnpm` field; it was moved here as the block's own comment prescribes, and `package.json` is unchanged.
- `pnpm-lock.yaml`: as pnpm wrote it (the patch hash on the `@better-auth/scim` snapshot).
- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/scim-name-recompose.test.ts` (new): the regression pin, every case through `AuthManager.handleRequest()` with a real SCIM bearer on a real ObjectQL over better-sqlite3.

No changeset, `skip-changeset`: the published `@objectstack/plugin-auth` tarball (`files: dist, README.md, CHANGELOG.md`) is byte-for-byte what it was; `@better-auth/scim` is an external dependency of its bundle, and a pnpm patch applies only to installs of THIS workspace (dev, CI, and the framework build base image built from it), never to an npm install of the published package. A changelog line would tell npm consumers about a fix their install does not get. Measured, see Verification.

## Read first (by risk)

1. `patches/@better-auth__scim@1.7.12.patch`, the `setNamePart` hunk: the derived test is a VALUE test (`state.formattedName === composeName(state)`, read BEFORE the assignment). That line decides every case below, including the edge one.
2. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/scim-name-recompose.test.ts`, case (c): the edge where the value test and the vendor's own suite disagree.
3. `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, the `patchedDependencies` note: what removes the patch.

## Tests

- (a) Entra path-addressed (`Replace` on `name.givenName` and `name.familyName`) and Okta path-less (`replace` with dotted keys): `displayName`, `name.formatted` and `sys_user.name` move to the new parts; an unrelated PATCH (`title`) afterwards keeps the new name (the vendor rewrites `sys_user.name` from its stored `displayName` on every profile PATCH).
- (b) CONTROLS: an explicit `displayName` (which seeds `name.formatted` at create) survives a part change; an explicit `name.formatted` survives, with the `displayName` derived from it; a `displayName` set by an earlier PATCH survives while the derived `name.formatted` moves; a `displayName` sent in the same PATCH as the parts wins, in both operation orders.
- (c) EDGE: a `displayName` and `name.formatted` supplied explicitly but EQUAL to the composed parts read as derived and move. Pinned on purpose, so the upgrade PR that removes the patch reads the reversal (Acceptance notes).

## Acceptance notes

- **The value test reverses one vendor-pinned case.** `@better-auth/scim`'s own suite at `v1.7.12` (and at `main`, 1.7.28) carries `preserves explicitly supplied formatted and display names when patching one name part`: create with `displayName` and `name.formatted` both `Ada Lovelace` and parts Ada / Lovelace, PATCH `name.givenName` to Augusta, expect both names kept. The vendor stores no record of whether a name was supplied or composed, so the ruled test (the value test `setFormattedName` already makes) reads that shape as derived and recomposes it to `Augusta Lovelace`; case (c) pins it. Every explicit name that differs from the parts is still kept (b). The upstream draft below changes that vendor test's fixture to an explicit name that differs from the parts; if the vendor wants the equal case preserved, the only fix is a persisted provenance bit, which is a larger vendor change.
- **Who receives the fix.** Every install of this workspace, so every image built from the framework build base and every dev and CI run. An npm install of the published `@objectstack/plugin-auth` resolves an unpatched `@better-auth/scim` until the vendor ships the recompose (ruling item 3).
- **Not covered by the value test.** A user created with no name parts has `name.formatted` = the primary email; a later PATCH that adds parts does not recompose it (the email is not composed from parts). Removing both parts one by one leaves `name.formatted` on the last single part (`composeName` of nothing is empty, and an empty name is never written).
- `pnpm patch-commit` writes `patchedDependencies` into `package.json`'s `pnpm` field, duplicating the three existing rows there; the comment in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` already says to move it, which this PR did.

## Verification

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/scim-name-recompose.test.ts` after `pnpm install` and a build of `@objectstack/plugin-auth`'s dependencies; expect `Tests  8 passed (8)`. Then delete the `@better-auth/scim@1.7.12` row from `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `pnpm install`, re-run: expect `6 failed | 2 passed (8)`.

It is NOT MEASURED on the final head; CI runs it. `check:test-source-alias` was red on the first draft of the new test (the SSO egress guard loaded inside a case) and is green after the module-top import.

Published-content check (positive control included): after building `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, the patched line occurs in 0 files of its `dist/`, while `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.mjs` import `@better-auth/scim` as an external dependency, so the tarball carries the vendor as a reference and none of its code.

## Upstream draft (for the maintainer to submit)

Against `better-auth/better-auth` `main` (8c5c68010b, `packages/scim` 1.7.28, where `setNamePart` is unchanged from 1.7.12). Agents cannot open it; NOT MEASURED against the vendor's own suite (its workspace was not installed here), so run `pnpm --filter @better-auth/scim test` before submitting.

**Title:** fix(scim): recompose derived name.formatted and displayName when a name part changes

**Description:** A SCIM User PATCH that replaces only `name.givenName` and/or `name.familyName` (Microsoft Entra ID sends one path-addressed `Replace` per part; Okta sends a path-less `replace` whose value carries `name.givenName` / `name.familyName` keys) updates the parts but leaves `name.formatted`, `displayName` and the backing Better Auth user's `name` on the old name. `setNamePart` stores the part and never recomposes, while `composeName` is used only by the `name.formatted` remove path, so an identity provider whose attribute mapping sends only the parts keeps showing the old name indefinitely; only a `displayName` PATCH or a full PUT moves it. This change recomposes `name.formatted` in `setNamePart` when it equalled `composeName` of the parts before the change, and lets `setFormattedName` carry `displayName` along when that was derived from `name.formatted`, the same derived-value test `setFormattedName` already makes. A formatted or display name that differs from the parts is never overwritten. One existing test changes: `preserves explicitly supplied formatted and display names when patching one name part` used an explicit name equal to the composed parts, which the stored state cannot tell from a derived one; its fixture now uses explicit names that differ from the parts, so it still pins preservation.
